paper.title: The Single-Copy Quantum Bandit Is Classical: An Exact Spectral Collapse

settings.name_in_paper: States-as-arms quantum bandit with single-copy policies (Pi_1)
unmapped: each arm supplies a fresh copy of an unknown quantum state rho_k on a d-dimensional Hilbert space
learner chooses an arbitrary (adaptive, randomized) finite-outcome POVM per copy and observes only the measurement outcome
mean reward mu_k = Tr(rho_k F) for a known effect F with finite spectrum (alphabet size L)
settings.definition_quote: An instance is $\nu=(\rho_1,\dots,\rho_K)\in\D(\mathcal H)^K$ with means $\mu_k=\Tr\rho_kF$, a unique best arm $k^\star$, $\mu^\star=\mu_{k^\star}$, and $0<\mu_k$ for all $k$, $\mu^\star<\lambda_{\max}(F)$. ... A single-copy policy ($\pi\in\Pi_1$): at round $t$ it selects an arm $A_t$ and a finite-outcome POVM $M_t$, both measurably (possibly at random) from the record ...

settings.name_in_paper: States-as-arms quantum bandit with quantum-memory policies (Pi_all)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Learner may store copies in quantum memory and apply joint quantum instruments (collective quantum measurements); quantum resource model outside classical bandit feedback.
unmapped: arms supply unknown quantum states; reward mean Tr(rho_k F) for known effect F
policies may store copies in a quantum register and apply arbitrary record-controlled quantum instruments jointly
settings.definition_quote: A quantum-memory policy ($\pi\in\Pi_{\mathrm{all}}$) may instead store copies in a quantum register and, in each round, apply an arbitrary record-controlled quantum instrument to the entire register before selecting the next arm; arm selection is a (possibly randomized) function of the classical record.

conditions: holds for adaptive and randomized measurement choice

source.label: thm:lbsc
source.quote: For every consistent $\pi\in\Pi_1$ and every suboptimal arm $k$, \[ \liminf_{T\to\infty}\ \frac{\mathbb E[N_k(T)]}{\ln T}\;\ge\;\frac{1}{\Minf(k)}\;=\;\frac{1}{\Kinf(k)}. \]

results.notes: Bound on expected pull count of each suboptimal arm. Kinf_i is the alphabet-restricted Burnetas-Katehakis functional of the spectral statistics of rho_k. Remark 3 extends this to policies storing copies for later single-copy measurement.

tuning: measure each copy with spectral POVM of F; threshold ln t + 3 ln ln t + (L-1)/2 ln n + c_L

source.label: thm:match
source.quote: Let \textsc{Spectral-KL-UCB} measure every pulled copy with the spectral POVM $\{P_i\}$ of $F$ and play the index policy of Section~\ref{sec:finite}. Then for every suboptimal $k$, $\limsup_T\mathbb E[N_k(T)]/\ln T\le1/\Kinf(k)$; combined with Theorem~\ref{thm:lbsc}, \[ \lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{R(T)}{\ln T}=\sum_{k\ne k^\star}\frac{\Delta_k}{\Kinf(k)} \]

results.notes: For projector F, Kinf_i = kl(mu_k, mu_star). Corollary 2 closes this via the finite-time theorem (same constant).

source.label: thm:match
source.quote: No consistent single-copy strategy --- adaptive, randomized, tomographic, or otherwise --- improves the leading constant over measuring the reward observable itself.

results.notes: Regret form of Theorem 2's lower bound, as stated in Theorem 3.

symbols.n_delta: smallest integer n >= max{1, ceil(a/b_k)} with n*b_k >= ln T + 3 ln ln T + (L-1)/2 ln n + c_L, where a=(L-1)/2, b_k = Kinf_k - delta_fin
symbols.L: number of distinct eigenvalues of the effect F (alphabet size)
symbols.eps_k: delta_fin / G_k, with G_k the subgradient bound of Lemma 2

source.label: thm:finite
source.quote: Under the model of Section~\ref{sec:model}, for every integer $T\ge3$, every suboptimal arm $k$ and every $\delta\in(0,\Kinf(q_k))$, with $G_k$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:dual} and $\varepsilon_k:=\delta/G_k$: \[ \mathbb E[N_k(T)]\ \le\ n_\delta(T)\;+\;\frac{2^L-2}{e^{\varepsilon_k^2/2}-1}\;+\;3. \]

results.notes: Bound on expected number of pulls of suboptimal arm k; regret follows by multiplying by Delta_k. Corollary 2: n_delta(T) = (ln T + O(ln ln T))/(Kinf - delta).

symbols.D_inf_i: inf over sigma with Tr(sigma F) >= mu_star of the Umegaki relative entropy D(rho_i || sigma)

source.label: thm:univ
source.quote: For every consistent $\pi\in\Pi_{\mathrm{all}}$ and suboptimal $k$, \[ \liminf_{T\to\infty}\ \frac{\mathbb E[N_k(T)]}{\ln T}\;\ge\;\frac{1}{\Dinf(k)}, \] and consequently $\liminf_T R(T)/\ln T\ge\sum_{k\ne k^\star}\Delta_k/\Dinf(k)$.

results.notes: Also gives per-arm pull-count bound log(T)/D_inf_k. D_inf = Kinf iff [rho_k, F]=0 (Corollary 4).
